newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ARSENAL-PSG FEUD OVER ANELKA RUMBLES ON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL-PSG FEUD OVER ANELKA RUMBLES ON.

text.p: Arsenal and Paris St Germain remained locked in a tug-of-war over teenage striker Nicolas Anelka on Tuesday while a Spanish newspaper claimed he had signed for Atletico Madrid.
"The situation hasn't changed since last Wednesday (when Arsenal confirmed the deal)," a spokeswoman for the English premier league side said. "As far as we're concerned he's still our player.
"He has every right to leave PSG and we see no reason why he won't be playing for Arsenal next season."
But PSG, who are anxious to keep the highly-rated 17-year-old on their books, have sent a dossier to the French Football Federation (FFF) asking officials to block any planned move to England.
Anelka, who is on an apprentice contract at present, needs permission from the FFF before he can leave PSG for a foreign club.
FFF president Claude Simonet confirmed he had received the PSG dossier and had given it to federation lawyers.
He did not disclose its contents and PSG declined to comment on the affair on Tuesday.
But PSG general manager Jean-Francois Domergue told sports daily L'Equipe the club would defend its interests as it had discovered and nurtured Anelka.
While Arsenal and PSG remained at loggerheads over the teenager, Spanish sports daily Marca reported he had agreed a deal with Spanish champions Atletico Madrid.
No one was available to comment at Atletico.
Anelka acknowledged in an interview with French newspaper Le Parisien last week he was unhappy at PSG, where he has failed to secure a regular first-team place.
He said he had signed a two-year deal with Arsenal.
"People don't show enough confidence in me (at PSG)," Anelka was reported as saying. "At Arsenal, I've been assured that I would be on level terms with the other forwards."
